voltage.note: Mean Well NGE12 05-USB (12 W wall adapter with a USB Type-A output, the 5 V model of the NGE12 series), SPECIFICATION p. 2: DC voltage 5 V, voltage tolerance +/-5.0%.

rInternal.note: Derived from the Mean Well NGE12 05-USB load regulation, +/-5.0% (SPECIFICATION p. 2): band +/-5% x 5 V = +/-0.25 V, whole swing up to 0.5 V over 0 to 2.4 A, 0.5 / 2.4 = 0.208 ohm, rounded to 0.21. Mean Well NGE12 SPECIFICATION p. 3, Note 6, reads "Load regulation is measured from 0% to 100% rated load"; the plus-minus figure is a band about the output at a reference load, so the whole 0 to rated-load swing can be up to twice the figure. This value uses that upper bound (real units usually droop less). The figure can be read two ways: 0.1 ohm (the +/-x% figure taken as the whole no-load to full-load swing) and 0.21 ohm (a band about a reference, up to twice the swing). 0.1 ohm is used: it is nearer typical droop, and this estimate never blocks.

imax.note: Mean Well NGE12 05-USB, SPECIFICATION p. 2: rated current 2.4 A, current range 0 to 2.4 A. Other 5 V USB chargers are commonly rated between 1 A and 3 A.

notes: The DC output is a source only when the converter is powered in the saved contact state (spec 4 table); otherwise it is open. That is solver logic, not data.
imax is the rated output current, compared as a rating; the module's own protection (NGE12 overload 110% to 150% of rated output power, hiccup mode) is not modelled.
The charger is generic; the Mean Well NGE12 05-USB (the module's own source) stands in for it. A cheaper charger may droop much more under load.
unaccounted: USB charger signalling on D+/D- (BC 1.2, Apple divider) is not modelled: devices see only VBUS.

corrected.why: load regulation +/-x% is a band about a reference output, so the 0 to rated-load swing can be up to 2x%; doubled (NGE12 Note 6: measured from 0% to 100% rated load)
